tickerText: [TENNIS] Wimbledon 2026 Day 7 Sunday, July 5: the fourth round opens at the All England Club after Saturday's shocks — Alexandra Eala became the first Filipino to reach a Grand Slam fourth round by stunning defending champion Iga Świątek 7-6 (11-9), 6-2 on Centre Court, Elise Mertens ousted Elena Rybakina 7-6 (7-4), 6-1, and Madison Keys beat Amanda Anisimova 3-6, 6-2, 6-3 — Centre Court Sunday features Novak Djokovic vs qualifier Roman Safiullin, Aryna Sabalenka vs Naomi Osaka, and defending champion Jannik Sinner vs Japanese qualifier Shintaro Mochizuki • [SQUASH] HCL-SRFI PSA Challenger crowned its champions Friday at Juhu Vile Parle Gymkhana in Mumbai — India's Tanvi Khanna rallied from two games down to beat Egypt's Farida Walid 8-11, 2-11, 12-10, 11-9, 11-7 for her fifth PSA title, while Malaysia's Mohammad Syafiq Kamal edged Yassin Shohdy 6-11, 9-11, 11-8, 14-12, 11-8 in a five-game men's final • [BADMINTON] YONEX Canada Open 2026 championship Sunday at Markham Pan Am Centre — Japan can complete a historic five-title sweep after Riki Takei ended Lee Zii Jia's run 13-21, 18-21, 21-18 in the semis, Yudai Okimoto halted home hope Victor Lai 15-21, 16-21, 11-21, Riko Gunji upset Michelle Li 13-21, 17-21, and representatives reached all five finals at the $250K BWF Super 300 • [PICKLEBALL] Sansan PPA Asia 500 Tokyo Open wraps at Arena Tachikawa Tachihi — Rika Fujiwara rallied past Pei Chuan Kao 7-11, 11-7, 12-10 for her second PPA Tour Asia singles gold, Yuta Funemizu and Tama Shimabukuro beat Collin Johns and Len Yang 8-11, 11-2, 11-7 in men's doubles, and Sahra Dennehy-Tama Shimabukuro completed a golden double with the mixed doubles title • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT United States Smash 2026 finals day at the Ontario Convention Center — South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin claimed their first WTT Grand Smash mixed doubles crown by beating Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha 11-9, 6-11, 7-11, 11-7, 11-8 on Friday, while Truls Möregårdh, Jang Woojin, Sun Yingsha, and Kanak Jha chase singles glory at the $1.55M Grand Smash through July 5

newsItems.title: Alexandra Eala Stuns Swiatek in Historic Wimbledon Upset
newsItems.excerpt: Filipina rising star Alexandra Eala produced the biggest win of her career on Saturday, July 4, toppling defending Wimbledon champion Iga Świątek 7-6 (11-9), 6-2 on Centre Court to become the first player from the Philippines to reach the fourth round of a Grand Slam in the Open era. The 21-year-old saved eight of 11 break points, hit 24 winners, and closed out a lengthy final game on her third match point as Świątek finished with 44 unforced errors. Eala, who beat Świątek at the 2025 Miami Open and won the Birmingham WTA 125 title on grass last month, dedicated the victory to "all the girls with ruffled socks and chubby cheeks" in an emotional on-court interview. Her win means no woman has successfully defended the Wimbledon singles title since Serena Williams in 2016. Eala will face 13th seed Jasmine Paolini in the Round of 16 on Monday, July 6, after Saturday also saw Elise Mertens eliminate second seed Elena Rybakina and Madison Keys defeat Amanda Anisimova in three sets.

newsItems.title: Japan Eyes Historic Sweep at Canada Open Finals
newsItems.excerpt: Japan has a chance to become the first nation since England in 2004 to sweep all five titles at the YONEX Canada Open 2026 as championship Sunday, July 5, arrives at the Markham Pan Am Centre. Saturday's semifinals delivered a wave of Japanese success: Riki Takei ended Paris 2024 bronze medallist Lee Zii Jia's title bid with a 13-21, 18-21, 21-18 comeback in 70 minutes to set up an all-Japanese men's singles final against Yudai Okimoto, who halted top-seeded Canadian Victor Lai 15-21, 16-21, 11-21 after Lai appeared hampered by a left knee problem. Riko Gunji upset four-time champion Michelle Li 13-21, 17-21 to reach the women's singles final against US Open winner Line Christophersen, who is into back-to-back World Tour finals for the first time. Japan are also guaranteed the women's doubles crown after Hinata Suzuki and Nao Yamakita, and Kaho Osawa and Mai Tanabe, advanced to the final. Chinese Taipei's Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin Hui reached the mixed doubles final a week after winning the US Open. The $250,000 BWF Super 300 concludes with five finals on a single show court.

newsItems.title: Fujiwara Rallies to Second Tokyo Open Singles Gold
newsItems.excerpt: Rika Fujiwara capped a memorable PPA Asia 500 Sansan Tokyo Open on Saturday, July 4, rallying from a set down to beat Pei Chuan Kao 7-11, 11-7, 12-10 and claim her second PPA Tour Asia women's singles title at Arena Tachikawa Tachihi. The 44-year-old, who became the first Japanese winner at May's Macau Open, saved match point at 10-10 in the decider before closing out the comeback in front of a raucous home crowd at Japan's first PPA Tour Asia stop. Earlier, Fujiwara and 15-year-old partner Kei Sawaki took women's doubles silver after falling to Sahra Dennehy and Danni Elle Townsend 4-11, 5-11. Yuta Funemizu and Tama Shimabukuro won the men's doubles crown with an 8-11, 11-2, 11-7 comeback over Collin Johns and Len Yang, and Dennehy later teamed with Shimabukuro to complete a golden double in mixed doubles by beating Yufei Long and Len Yang in straight games. The $50,000 event drew more than 800 players across five pro disciplines in the Japanese capital.

newsItems.title: Lim and Shin Claim First WTT Grand Smash Mixed Doubles Title
newsItems.excerpt: South Korea's Lim Jong-hoon and Shin Yu-bin finally broke through at the WTT United States Smash 2026, defeating world No. 1 pair Wang Chuqin and Sun Yingsha 11-9, 6-11, 7-11, 11-7, 11-8 in the mixed doubles final on Friday, July 4, at the Ontario Convention Center in Southern California. The top-seeded Koreans had reached three prior Grand Smash finals this year without winning, but rallied from a 2-1 deficit to deny the Olympic and world championship champions when Sun's final attack went wide. Lim and Shin, ranked first in the ITTF mixed doubles standings, add the $1.55 million event crown to their WTT Star Contender Ljubljana title from last month. On the singles side, defending men's champion Wang Chuqin and Lin Shidong were both eliminated in the Round of 16, leaving Kanak Jha as America's last men's hope, while Sun Yingsha advanced with a 11-8, 11-3, 11-5 win over Dina Meshref. The Grand Smash concludes Sunday, July 5, with men's and women's singles finals among the last trophies on the line.
